newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Oltchim plans bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Romania Oltchim plans bond issue.

text.p: Romanian chemical plant Oltchim, a first-tier listing on the Bucharest stock exchange, said on Monday it was planning to raise $50 million in bonds issued on the international market.

"We are now looking for a company to manage the issue," Oltchim economic manager Mandica Vasile told Reuters by phone from the company's headquarters in Rimnicu Vilcea, 175 km (109 miles) north-west of Bucharest.
"We will use the money, around $50 million, to complete investment programmes and re-equip the plant," he added.
Other details about the issue were not available.
The decision was reached during the company's latest shareholders' meeting, which also agreed in principle to raise Oltchim's capital by around five billion lei.
"We owed one of our shareholders, an investment company, dividends and they asked for shares instead," Vasile said.
Oltchim has a share capital of 267.1 billion lei, raised last year from 266.3 billion at end-1995 after recouping debts previously deducted from the capital base.

Other decisions made during the meeting included buying new equipment, taking a 20 billion lei banking credit to support export-oriented production and striking a small joint venture to produce PVC sheet with Germany's Balcke-Duerr AG.
The announcement ended a 20-minute suspension at the Monday session of the Bucharest bourse, where the stock is most heavily traded. It ended the session 100 lei firmer at 4,000.
Traders said the announcement would have an effect on the future prices of Oltchim, which they saw going up.
Last year, Oltchim posted a net profit of 22.8 billion lei, down from 23.6 billion in 1995. It said its profit had slipped due to heavy spending on companies with which it merged.

Romania re-entered international capital markets in 1995, after an absence of more than a decade, with syndicated loans for the National Bank (central bank), which also launched the first Samurai and Eurobond issues last year. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
